### Observed differences

- Activities A03 and A11 are no longer observed in the later window: A03 appeared in about 29 in 100 earlier traces (mean 1.16 occurrences per trace; 57 of 200 traces) and in 0 of 200 later traces; A11 appeared in about 20 in 100 earlier traces (mean 0.56; 39 of 200) and in 0 of 200 later traces. [OCC001, OCC002]
- The flow out of A06 changed completely: before, about 86 in 100 of A06's observed outgoing transitions went to A03 and about 7 in 100 to A11; after, none go to A03 or A11, while about 58 in 100 go to A19 and about 37 in 100 to A12 (A02 about 5 in 100). [DIR002]
- The disappeared activities' own connections are gone: A03's outgoing transitions (about 44 in 100 to A11, 28 to A19, 22 to A12) and A11's (about 97 in 100 back to A03) are unobserved after; before, A03 and A11 also repeatedly followed one another (A03 averaged 1.16 occurrences per trace, with A03–A11 interleaving in about 20 in 100 traces). [DIR001, DIR003, REL002]
- A03 no longer co-occurs with any former partner: co-occurrence with A06, A12, A19 and A11 fell from about 20–29 in 100 traces to 0, and A06 now appears without A03 in about 22 in 100 traces. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]
- A19 and A12 now occur earlier in the trace and closer to A06: each appears in about 22 in 100 later traces (down from about 29) at a mean position of about 0.22 versus about 0.32 before; A06 is immediately followed by A19 in about 24 in 100 observed pairs (about 2 in 100 before), and reaches A12 within one or two steps in about 40 in 100 pairs (about 18 before); the self-distances of A06, A12 and A19 moved from mostly four-to-five steps to mostly three-to-four. [POS003, POS004, LAG003, LAG002, LAG001, LAG004, LAG005]
- The affected branch is also exercised less: A06's observed outgoing transitions fell from 121 to 78. [DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis of a structural change in which the repeating A03–A11 block that previously sat between A06 and its outcomes is no longer executed, with A06 now bypassing it and leading directly to A19 and A12, which consequently appear earlier in traces. The signs are direct and mutually consistent: A03 and A11 fell from 57 and 39 of 200 traces to 0 of 200; A06's successor profile flipped from about 86 in 100 transitions to A03 to about 58 to A19 and 37 to A12; all A03 co-occurrences vanished; and the earlier positions and shorter lags of A19 and A12 match the loss of the intervening block. Screening tested 44 control-flow units and 18 items qualified, versus roughly 0.22 expected if nothing had changed, and every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits, so the set as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]. Limitations: zero participation shows only that A03 and A11 were not observed in the later sample, so a renaming or relabelling of these activities, or an after-window that contains none of the traces that used this loop, cannot be ruled out; the lag comparisons rest on modest samples (about 19–50 observed pairs each); and positions and lags measure event order, not clock time.

Other differences: the branch around A06 is exercised less often overall — A19 and A12 each appear in about 43 of 200 later traces versus 57 before, and A06's observed outgoing transitions fell from 121 to 78 — and A02's share of A06's outgoing transitions rose slightly (about 2 to about 5 in 100). [POS003, POS004, DIR002]
